title: Rhythm Pharmaceuticals Announces NICE Guidance for IMCIVREE® (Setmelanotide) Updated to Include Adults Living with Bardet-Biedl Syndrome
author: Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
description: Rhythm Pharmaceuticals announced that the UK's National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) has expanded its positive guidance for IMCIVREE (setmelanotide) to include adults with genetically confirmed Bardet-Biedl syndrome, allowing NHS funding for this patient population. The expansion builds on previous 2024 guidance that covered patients ages 6-17 and recognizes the significant burden of hyperphagia and obesity associated with the disease throughout adulthood.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: NICE expanded reimbursement eligibility for IMCIVREE to adults with Bardet-Biedl syndrome, broadening the addressable patient population and NHS funding access in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland. This represents regulatory progress and increased commercial opportunity for the company's lead asset.

title: Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (RYTM) Reports Q3 Loss, Beats Revenue Estimates
author: Zacks.Com
description: Rhythm Pharmaceuticals reported a Q3 loss of $0.61 per share, beating consensus estimates of $0.68 loss, with a 10.29% earnings surprise. Revenue reached $92.13 million, surpassing estimates by 9.07% and nearly doubling year-ago revenues of $51.3 million. However, the stock has underperformed the market, down 12.7% year-to-date versus the S&P 500's 10.2% gain. The company holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with mixed estimate revisions.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the company beat both EPS and revenue estimates with strong revenue growth (79% YoY), the stock has significantly underperformed the market year-to-date (-12.7% vs S&P 500 +10.2%). The Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating and mixed estimate revisions suggest neutral near-term performance expectations despite positive earnings results.

Techne is expected to report earnings with modest growth (9.5% YoY EPS growth, 2.4% revenue growth). Consensus estimates have been revised slightly higher (1.2%) over the last 30 days, indicating stable but unspectacular performance expectations.

title: Rhythm Pharmaceuticals and LG Chem Enter into Amendment to Bivamelagon Exclusive License Agreement
author: Na
description: Rhythm Pharmaceuticals amended its global licensing agreement with LG Chem for bivamelagon, reducing royalties from low-to-mid-single digits to 1% on MC4R agonist sales while committing to $350 million in fixed payments over four years. The company also secured a $750 million term-loan facility led by KKR's HealthCare Royalty and Blackstone to support the agreement, commercialization efforts, and pipeline development.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The company secured substantial financing ($750M) and renegotiated favorable terms with LG Chem, reducing variable royalties to a fixed 1% rate while gaining access to capital for commercialization and R&D. This demonstrates financial flexibility and confidence in its MC4R portfolio's potential.

HealthCare Royalty leads a $750 million term-loan facility with favorable terms (SOFR + 4.60%, no equity component, no pre-maturity amortization), positioning the firm to benefit from Rhythm's commercial success in a high-potential therapeutic area.

title: Rhythm Pharmaceuticals Announces Commercial Launch of IMCIVREE® (setmelanotide) in Japan for Patients with Acquired Hypothalamic Obesity
author: Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
description: Rhythm Pharmaceuticals announced the commercial launch of IMCIVREE (setmelanotide) in Japan following MHLW approval and inclusion on Japan's National Health Insurance drug price list. IMCIVREE is the first approved therapy in Japan for acquired hypothalamic obesity, with an estimated patient population of 5,000-8,000 people. The approval was supported by Phase 3 TRANSCEND trial data showing an 18.8% placebo-adjusted BMI reduction.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The company successfully launched its lead asset IMCIVREE in a new major market (Japan) following regulatory approval and NHI reimbursement listing. This represents significant commercial expansion and market access for a rare disease treatment with an estimated addressable population of 5,000-8,000 patients. The approval validates the drug's efficacy demonstrated in clinical trials.
